body:
The BuildTest coordinator teardown work began with the owner asking, “Do we really have 135 droplets stuck in tearing down?” Its deterministic in-memory fixtures found that FakeFileSystem could lose a child that another caller had already written and closed: createDirectory looked up an absent entry, invoked the public clock, and then replaced a directory created during that callback with a fresh empty instance. This change is part of the BuildTest utilization / projections campaign tracked in url://handoff/handoffs/hf-2026-08-24-fix-startup-compaction-delta-heap-exhaustion-then-revalidate-the-extreme-suite .

The [consumer reproduction](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/BuildTestEmbedded/tree/wip/teardownfix1-evidence/evidence/teardownfix1/directory-proof-exact-core) establishes this second, separate defect in the previously published registry fix. This PR adds the compatible 3.4.0 sources to the organization's existing backport build pattern, preserves existing directories, and holds the registry lock across directory lookup, existence checks and insertion. Clock reads happen before that transaction and their value is reused through root and symlink lookup. Must-create calls reject an existing entry; ordinary directory creation also preserves files by reporting an error rather than replacing them.

The authorized artifact is published as `com.squareup.okio:okio-fakefilesystem-jvm:3.4.0-r576-registry-lock-2` on [kotlin.directory](https://kotlin.directory/com/squareup/okio/okio-fakefilesystem-jvm/3.4.0-r576-registry-lock-2/okio-fakefilesystem-jvm-3.4.0-r576-registry-lock-2.pom). The published JAR is the exact file tested by the gate (SHA-256 `21e60aadff3bf4906847103742c28b6a197349ecf58f132bd4eebf07e4c9e7a4`). Its class names and every public JVM signature match -1 in `javap`; its POM retains all prior dependency versions. The repeatable build checks those conditions before producing the artifact.

Validation:

- Red-first: all nine public directory scenarios fail 3/3 against the exact served -1 dependency and consumer core 3.4.0.2: 27/27 assertion failures, zero errors/skips.
- Product-only mutation control: restoring the prior directory implementation gives 27/27 directory assertion failures while all four registry neighbours pass. The source, native XML and complete traces are on the [separate evidence branch](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/okiofakefs1-evidence/evidence/okiofakefs1).
- [Final exact-source GitHub gate](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/actions/runs/39004533954): 27/27 directory first attempts pass, plus all four registry neighbours. The r576 workload retains 20 trials, nine callers and 10,000 operations per caller: 20/20 trials pass, all 1.8 million operations complete. Native XML contains 31 successful first-attempt rows, zero failures/errors/skips and no retry history.
- The directory cases cover the supplied callback proof, two-thread child preservation, concurrent must-create admission, existing directories/files, callback must-create, roots and symlink parents. Independent test and code review passes are recorded in the evidence findings.
- Both served files return HTTP 200 and match the tested JAR/POM hashes. No additional positive test batch ran after the gate.

Existing-test edits: none. The historical registry callback and snapshot test source is copied without changes; the original registry workload counts are preserved. No timeout or iteration count was changed. The temporary validation workflow exists only on its separate `wip/gha-run/okiofakefs1` branch. The orchestrator owns the PR's full-suite CI and merge decision; this PR is not merged or queued.
